- Model consistently underestimates prices in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates prices after sharp upward spikes in recent history (e.g., 88+ → 85+ → 80+), often overshooting by 2–5%.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the middle-to-late forecast period (days 15–25), failing to capture mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly after volatility spikes.
- Underreacts to recent low prices (e.g., 75–78 range) and overreacts to minor rebounds, leading to overcorrection in the 20–25 day window.
- When history includes a strong recent peak, model fails to adjust downward sufficiently, creating a “false plateau” effect.
- Forecast error is more pronounced when true outcome is below 80, especially if preceded by a high recent value.
